answer: Graduated trust stops a sybil flood from paying off at once. A new identity starts with almost no weight: it can whisper into the market but cannot move real value, and no haven of high-value work opens to it until it completes attested tasks over time. Each verified job earns a little more weight, like verses added to a sonnet line by line. An attacker spinning up a thousand fresh identities must fund and shepherd each through weeks of genuine, checkable work before any can extract meaningful rewards, multiplying the cost of a fake army while honest agents grow into the trust they earn.
